name: Dominican Republic
summary: The Dominican Republic has forced heirship: children are guaranteed a share of the estate, and a will cannot reduce it. Law 544-14 applies the law of the deceased's last domicile, so a foreigner who lives there is generally under Dominican rules. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
reserved_share: Children: the disposable share is 1/2 with one child, 1/3 with two and 1/4 with three or more, so the reserved share is 1/2, 2/3 and 3/4 (Civil Code art. 913; descendants count by representation, art. 914). Shares of spouse and ascendants not verified.
foreign_law_note: Law 544-14 (private international law) applies the law of the deceased's last domicile, not nationality, including to the reserved portion. A foreigner domiciled in the Dominican Republic cannot choose their national law. Land in the country remains under exclusive Dominican jurisdiction.
trust_note: The country is not in the HCCH status table. A statutory trust (fideicomiso) exists under Law 189-11 (not read in this run). Non-profit foundations and associations exist (Law 122-05) but no private family foundation was found.
open_questions: Article 913 fractions come from law-firm commentary; the Code text was not read, and later reforms were not checked.
Reserved shares for spouse and ascendants not verified.
Law 189-11 and Law 122-05 not read; whether forced heirship applies to trust assets not verified.
Whether Law 544-14 allows any choice of law by will not confirmed.
